completed_milestones.summary: Environment audit, architecture and decision records, seven v1 contracts with examples and tests, olb CLI (validate, diagnose, check, state), roadmap and agent instructions.

World source tree with two working capabilities (text.stats, math.evaluate), a build-time capability invoker, olb world build and olb world verify, the digest algorithm, invocation protocol and data root default documented in CONTRACTS.md.

Simulation bootstrap: experiment manager, supervisor with deadline and process-tree termination, single hash-chained recorder, tool host, agent loop behind a ModelClient interface with a scripted stand-in, workspace artifact scanning, ols run and ols verify. No model is called.

Chat model client over Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint with tool calling, tool-call repair, retry, context guard and recorded model identity; ols measure-model; llama3.2:3b measured and recorded in minimal world 0.2.0; one documented real-model run whose archive verifies.

Window bootstrap and first version: loopback-only standard-library server with a JSON API and a static front end (no build step). Run list, run summary with frozen configuration, paginated timeline with type filters, tool call and result pairs, artifact previews, live tail by polling, event-log check against the archive's own schemas and hash chain. Read-only guarantees are tested. Front-end stack decided (ADR-0008).

A reply without a tool call no longer ends a run: the runtime answers with the experiment's continuation message (default text in experiment-config 1.1.0), recorded as an environment.message event (observation-event 1.1.0); the context guard drops whole old turns and records it. Three candidate orchestrators (qwen3.5:2b, qwen3:4b, granite4.1:3b) pulled with authorisation, measured, recorded in minimal world 0.3.0 and compared with llama3.2:3b in eight archived open-trial runs. The Window renders environment.message.

Deterministic registry index, weighted pure-Python keyword search, complete generated capability documentation and three new simple capabilities (workspace.write, workspace.list, time.now). Minimal world 0.4.0 built, self-tested, verified and published; Simulation fixture rebuilt/copied, experiments updated and shipped tools tested (72c78d8). Scripted file-writing archive verified and text artifact inspected in the Window without changing archive bytes (9ef9ba4). Runtime discovery remains S005b.

Four discovery meta-tools backed by the built registry and generated documentation; restricted search/describe and permission-checked real demonstrations/invocations. Generic recorded system preamble (observation-event 1.2.0, minimal world 0.5.0). Context guard preserves fresh tool results and both initial messages; original tool-call arguments are archived separately from recorded syntactic repairs. Scripted acceptance passes; final directed llama3.2:3b trial archives a successful search/describe/invoke sequence with no tool names in its initial prompt. Earlier failures retained; no autonomous reliability claim.

Durable SQLite memory capabilities in minimal world 0.6.0; working-notes convention; complete-step checkpoint barriers with conversation, runtime cursor/counters, SQLite backup and workspace ZIP; validated atomic publication, retention and cooperative pause/ols resume. Resume preserves the log and artifact history, falls back from corruption and retains original time/step budgets while excluding downtime. ADR-0009 refines live memory location and append-only rollback; checkpoint-metadata 1.0.1 clarifies the boundary. Scripted/CLI and fake-model acceptance verified; automatic crash/stale-lock recovery and graceful deadline checkpointing remain S006b.

The original supervisor milestone was split before implementation: S006b graceful deadlines, S006d recovery, S006e resource enforcement. Bounded checkpoint_then_stop requires checkpointing, uses one fixed grace allowance, snapshots at a complete-step barrier and kills before acknowledgement. Expiry/timeouts preserve prior safe checkpoints; post-kill barriers cannot snapshot. Original budgets remain unchanged. Scripted native CLI archive verifies; 159 Simulation and 305 Builder tests pass. ADR-0010 documents semantics and limits. Automatic recovery and resource enforcement remain unimplemented.

Opt-in bounded runtime recovery under one long-lived supervisor; shared persisted restart budget, pre-execution model-attempt reservations and active-time ledger; permanent OS writer guard with hashed installation/PID/birth identity and safe stale-marker retention; ols recover startup scan for opted-in interrupted runs; asynchronous model identity/availability probes. Native worker and exact-supervisor fault injection, append-only restoration, downtime accounting and refusal paths verified. 188 Simulation tests and 305 Builder tests pass. ADR-0011 documents extension semantics and limits. Resource enforcement remains S006e; no OS startup task installed; physical reboot/power-loss, Linux execution and large-run host I/O remain unverified.

Aggregate Windows Job Object RAM/process-count/CPU cycle ceilings, suspended startup before job assignment, supervisor workspace quota admission and active-writer checks, periodic supervisor resource samples with unavailable fields and optional host NVIDIA VRAM used/available. Unsupported/unrepresentable limits are refused, including VRAM, nested wall clock and unenforced model-token limits. Native resource faults, CPU cap/throttle, startup ordering, quota/read admission, resume and failures verified. 214 Simulation and 305 Builder tests pass; shipped CLI and quota archives verify. ADR-0012 documents cycle/active-time differences, polling overshoot and best-effort notifications. Completes the split S006b/S006d/S006e process supervisor scope; container isolation remains human-gated.

known_issues.summary: WSL status is unresponsive and no container engine is available on the development machine.
known_issues.detail: S006e read-only wsl.exe --status timed out after ten seconds; neither Podman nor Docker was found. S006c requires human repair/engine approval. No system change or workaround was attempted; the roadmap explicitly allows proceeding to S007a.

known_issues.summary: FFmpeg and PyTorch are not installed.
The development machine is a laptop on a pre-release Windows build; sleep, updates and reboots will interrupt long runs.
known_issues.detail: S006d recovery is implemented and tested with native process termination; physical reboot and host suspend/resume remain unverified. Power and update settings need review before multi-hour runs.

known_issues.summary: World builds, the content digest, process-tree termination and the Window have only been run on Windows.
known_issues.detail: The digest hashes stored bytes and the repository forces LF line endings, so it should be identical on Linux. The Simulation kills the run's process tree with a Job Object on Windows and a process group on POSIX; only the Windows path has been exercised. Check both the first time a Linux environment is available. The Window uses only pathlib and the standard-library HTTP server and should behave the same on Linux; its tests have not been run there. SQLite memory, checkpoint ZIP/backup, resume and writer-lock tests have also only run on Windows. S006d native OS writer locks, process birth identity, worker/supervisor termination and startup recovery have been exercised on Windows only. Mocked Linux identity branches are tested, but no Linux OS execution occurred. S006e job ceilings, suspended startup, CPU throttling, quota admission and resource samples were tested on Windows only. Non-Windows CPU/RAM/process limits are explicitly refused; optional unavailable samples are marked rather than fabricated.

known_issues.summary: On the process tier nothing stops a capability process from reading or writing outside the workspace.
known_issues.detail: The Simulation gives capabilities an empty environment and only tells them the workspace path, but that is a convention for Builder-written capabilities, not enforcement. The supervisor re-checks the world digest after each run. Real enforcement arrives with the container tier (S006c).

known_issues.summary: No local candidate that fits the 4 GB GPU behaves as an autonomous tool user under an unprompted premise.
known_issues.detail: Runs no longer end at the first reply without a tool call (S003c), but llama3.2:3b mostly applies text.stats to the text it was given and invents surroundings, and the other candidates ask for a task. See docs/experiments/2026-11-14-orchestrator-candidates.md and OD-2. S005b reached a bounded directed search/describe/invoke acceptance sequence with explicitly guided argument structure and recorded repairs; eleven debugging trials varied prompts and runtime, so they do not establish reliable or unprompted autonomy. See docs/experiments/2026-11-14-discovery-meta-tools.md.

known_issues.summary: The context window in use is Ollama's default of 4096 tokens, and the server-reported input token count is not the conversation length.
known_issues.detail: The OpenAI-compatible endpoint cannot set the context size per request. Since S003c the runtime blanks old tool results and then drops whole old turns (never the initial prompt), recording both, so nothing is cut silently; but with 4096 tokens the conversation keeps only a few recent turns. Long runs need a larger context (server setting or the native API) and memory. S005b preserves the system preamble, initial user prompt and newest assistant/tool group. Fresh documentation is never blanked before its first use; protected content can still exceed the conservative estimate.

known_issues.summary: Real image artifact previews remain unverified; synthetic image archives are tested.
known_issues.detail: S005a checked a real scripted workspace.write artifact in the Window: list metadata and preserved text preview displayed correctly, all 16 archive files were unchanged after browsing, and ols verify passed. No shipped capability creates an image yet. See docs/experiments/2026-11-14-registry-artifacts.md.

known_issues.summary: The Window cannot tell a run in progress from one that was interrupted, and its front end has no automated tests.
known_issues.detail: The Window still shows a run without summary.json as not finished, using the last recorded state/event time. S006d adds host-local writer/accounting files and recovery actions, but the Window does not interpret them as liveness evidence. JSON API/read-only guarantees are tested; the front end still has no automated rendering tests.

known_issues.summary: Thinking models spend most of their output budget on reasoning the record never sees, and it cannot be switched off through the endpoint in use.
known_issues.detail: max_output_tokens covers the hidden reasoning: qwen3:4b at 512 produced only empty replies. Asking Ollama 0.40.16 for reasoning_effort 'none' moved the reasoning into the reply text, which would be recorded as said, so the runtime sends no such option. If a thinking model is chosen (OD-2) the protocol must say how much unrecorded computation is acceptable.

known_issues.summary: Recovery is opt-in; physical reboot/power-loss durability, Linux execution and large-run timing remain unverified.
known_issues.detail: S006d passes native Windows worker/exact-supervisor termination and startup recovery tests. ols recover is an explicit startup scan; no OS boot task was installed. Interrupted accounting uses durable one-second reservations, not an inferred exact death time. Partial observation/artifact writes, invalid accounting and unverifiable legacy/foreign ownership are refused rather than repaired by inference. Uninterruptible host I/O and directory-entry power-loss durability are not guaranteed. See ADR-0011 and docs/experiments/2026-11-14-supervisor-recovery.md.

known_issues.summary: Resource enforcement retains process-tier limits: disk quota may overshoot during a write and Windows notification delivery is best effort.
known_issues.detail: OS job RAM/process ceilings and CPU cycle rate are installed independently of notification delivery. CPU active-time samples are not exact short-window equivalents of nominal core cycle budgets. Supervisor disk checks deny future writing calls at quota and kill an observed live writer above quota, but do not impose an OS byte quota or limit archive/model storage. GPU samples are host-wide; VRAM limits and non-Windows CPU/RAM/process limits are refused. Uninterruptible host I/O, physical reboot/power-loss and Linux execution remain unverified. See ADR-0012 and docs/experiments/2026-11-14-resource-enforcement.md.

open_decisions.summary: Container mechanism for the container isolation tier (Podman in WSL 2 preferred).
open_decisions.detail: Decide once WSL is repaired and the options can be tested. ADR-0006.

open_decisions.summary: Which orchestrator model to use. Four models that fit the 4 GB GPU have been compared; none behaves as an autonomous tool user unprompted.
open_decisions.detail: Evidence in docs/experiments/2026-11-14-orchestrator-candidates.md. llama3.2:3b uses tools most but invents surroundings; qwen3:4b is grounded but needs about 2048 output tokens per reply (hidden reasoning, about 30 s per step); qwen3.5:2b and granite4.1:3b act as assistants waiting for a user. Options: keep llama3.2:3b, adopt qwen3:4b with a larger output limit, authorise a larger partially offloaded model (e.g. qwen3.5:4b or qwen3.5:9b), or enable an external provider (ADR-0005). Worth repeating after S005b, when the world has more tools. Deferred by the human on 2026-11-14: llama3.2:3b stays the default for now. Planned later: try a larger model, and a 'brain swap' mode that can use an external provider with the human's own API key (a frontier model, or a hosted Gemma model) - see the note under S007a in ROADMAP.md.
